disagreements.positions: A1 and A3 use 5.0x (+6%) on the SCA floor. A2 and A4 use 5.1x (+8%) on the SCAs plus the Korea discount. A5 uses 5.0x on the SCAs, the US listing and MU's own peak-cycle average.
disagreements.resolution: The SCAs are not MU-specific. Samsung targets 60-70% of memory capacity under 5-year LTAs, some with floor prices and deposits. SK hynix has about 10 customers on LTAs with purchase commitments and deposits, with minimum-price clauses and 10-30% prepayments reported for Microsoft and Google. The floor is a sector-wide change that peer multiples already reflect. What does persist and is documented is a US-listing premium: Sandisk trades at 8.0x NTM against 4.3x for Kioxia, its fab JV partner, and MU has traded above SK hynix and Samsung through past cycles. I allow ~9% over 4.5x, which gives 4.9x. That is slightly below the agents' 5.0-5.1x, and it rests on a different basis (see cyclicality_review).

They are real (primary text) but sector-wide (Samsung 60-70% LTA coverage, SK hynix ~10 customers), and the floor covers only ~$14/sh a year of earnings against ~$200 of peak EPS.
Supply-wave timing: Micron ID1 and Tongluo mid-2027, SK hynix Y1 Feb-2027, Samsung P5 1H27, then Japan, ID2 and Singapore NAND from late 2028. FY27 capex is >$50B and construction-heavy.

comps_review.premium_verdict: Every agent's 5.0-5.1x was justified as a 6-8% premium to a 4.7x median that was itself inflated by a double NTM adjustment. Against the true 4.5x it is an 11-13% premium. The stated basis (the SCA floor) is not MU-specific, because Samsung and SK hynix run the same take-or-pay and deposit LTAs. A US-listing premium is the persistent, documented part (Sandisk 8.0x against JV partner Kioxia 4.3x), and it supports ~9%, so 4.9x. 5.0x is borderline acceptable. 5.1x is an unjustified premium.

cyclicality_review.question: Do the 26 take-or-pay SCAs (>35% of revenue through 2030), ~$150B of RPO and the deposits make MU less cyclical enough to deserve a multiple above the memory-peer median?
cyclicality_review.what_is_verified: From the primary prepared remarks (30 Sep 2026): the agreements are explicitly 'multi-year take-or-pay', and 'all SCAs have take-or-pay contracted volumes'. Three-quarters of SCA revenue has a defined pricing framework, mostly floor and ceiling bands; the rest reprices to market. RPO of ~$150B counts committed volumes at minimum prices only. Customer commitments are $32B, mostly cash, with $12.7B of deposits held, unrestricted, and returned in the latter half of each term if minimums are met. Management says margins even at floor prices are 'meaningfully above any prior cycle peak'. Some SCAs run into 2031.
cyclicality_review.how_much_it_protects: $150B over ~4.25 years (Oct-26 to 2030) is ~$35B a year at floor prices, ~13% of FY27 consensus revenue ($275B). At a floor operating margin of ~55% and 15.5% tax, that is ~$16B of net income, or ~$14/sh a year, against ~$200 of FY28 EPS: about 7% of peak earnings is contractually floored. Deposits are ~$11/sh. The other ~65% of revenue, plus the market-repriced quarter of SCA revenue, keeps full price exposure, and ceilings cap upside on part of the contracted book. Effect on the trough: it lifts the floor of trough EPS and FCF (the agents' DCFs keep FY30 FCF positive, which is reasonable). Effect on the multiple compression the stock usually suffers before peak EPS (2018: -57% from ~4.5x forward): little.
cyclicality_review.durability: Contract durability is untested. Pre-2023 memory LTAs were one-year, locked-volume and floating-price, and buyers 'treated them as scrap paper' when demand fell. The new deals carry deposits and take-or-pay penalties, which analysts call 'mutual hostage-taking' that softens but does not end the cycle (SK Securities, via Korea Herald). Renegotiation in a deep downturn remains plausible.
cyclicality_review.sector_wide_or_mu_specific: Sector-wide. Samsung targets 60-70% of medium- to long-term memory capacity under 5-year LTAs with advance payments and some floor prices. SK hynix has ~10 customers under LTAs with purchase commitments and deposits, including reported minimum-price clauses and 10-30% prepayments for Microsoft and Google (Korea Herald, 2 and 12 Aug 2026; itiger). Samsung's coverage target exceeds MU's >35%. Any de-rating of memory cyclicality therefore lifts the whole group, and today's ~4.5x peer median already prices it.
cyclicality_review.verdict: Yes, the evidence shows memory has become somewhat less cyclical in its trough economics: higher earnings floor, prepaid cash, better visibility. No, it does not justify a multiple above the memory-peer median for MU on cyclicality grounds, because the same structure is in place at Samsung and SK hynix (and the NAND names) and is reflected in their ~4.5x. The floor covers only ~7% of peak EPS. MU's premium is granted on the documented US-listing gap (~9%, giving 4.9x), not on the SCAs. The SCAs belong in the bull scenario (a sector-wide re-rating to 6-7x) and in a positive trough FCF, not in the base multiple.

round2_review.what_changed_round1_to_round2: Mean fair value fell from $1,028.6 to $1,003.8. Mean P(>= $1,075) fell from 0.492 to 0.474. Thesis breaks were rebuilt from post-print numbers ($600-660, mean $615). All agents fixed the real round-1 errors: trailing EV/EBITDA labelled as forward, A4's buyback and share-count error, A2's understated cash, A5's double-counted deposits, and the circular 5.5x.
round2_review.herding: Dispersion collapsed. The ladder range across agents at K = $1,290 shrank from 0.105 to 0.037, and at $1,451 from 0.074 to 0.022. All five adopted the round-1 supervisor's peer numbers verbatim (4.65/4.73/5.4/4.2/7.8) and set multiples just under its 5.2x cap. Convergence on verified primary facts is good. Convergence on an unverified restatement is not, and that restatement turned out to be wrong. So the tight round-2 agreement on the multiple carries less independent information than it appears to.
round2_review.independence_check: Lanes were kept, with distinct shares in source_overlap: 0.634 distinct URLs, mean Jaccard 0.22. But the valuation anchor (peer comps) came from a single vendor plus a single supervisor transformation for every agent.
round2_review.net_effect: The correction lowers fair value ~3%, from ~$1,004 to ~$970, and shifts the base and bull band of the ladder ~0.01-0.02 down. The cyclicality evidence is real but sector-wide, so it moves nothing at the MU-specific level.

summary: Every company figure checks out against the 8-K and prepared remarks, and the SCAs are explicitly take-or-pay ($150B RPO at minimum prices, $12.7B deposits). Samsung and SK hynix have struck the same kind of deals, though, and the floor protects only ~7% of peak EPS. That softens memory's trough but does not justify a multiple above the peer median. All five agents built on a peer median of 4.7x that double-adjusted vendor figures already on an NTM basis. The consistent NTM median is ~4.5x P/E and ~3.5x EV/EBITDA, so corrected fair value is ~$970 (~10% below spot) with a median near $1,040. The ladder sits ~0.02 below the agent mean above $967. The open question is still when in 2027 the market starts pricing the 2028 supply wave.
